text:
sara: heads up — seeing p95 east-west RTTs spike from ~4ms to ~65-110ms across GPU pods in rack-8 during the 17:00-17:30 batching window. dashboards: https://redwood.internal/d/ewlatency
noah: seeing that too. packet loss ~0.8% on inter-node path on the same time slices. alerted infra-bot.
infra-bot: ALERT: cluster-us-east-1 / rack-8 / EW_LINK_P95 above threshold (65ms) 
anya: did we push the MTU tweak to rack-8 last night? I remember a partial jumbo enable landed in the Ansible run.
matt: yep, `playbook: network/jumbo-frames` touched tor-8 and all nodes but we rolled back to test on tor-5 only. check `git rev-parse --short HEAD` -> 8b3f2a4.
noah: running quick `ssh node-gpu-8-4 'ip -s link show eth0'` shows rx errors bumping during spike window. snippet: ```3: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 rx: 1.2M packets, 12 errs tx: 1.2M packets, 0 errs```
anya: if MTU mismatch between ToR and host that can cause fragmentation and retransmits when batch bursts saturate the qdisc. could be intermittent because we only partially rolled out.
sara: can someone run an RDMA health check? `ibstat`/`ibv_devinfo` on node-gpu-8-*.
matt: ran `ibv_devinfo` on 8-2 and 8-6; firmware mismatch on 8-6 (v41 vs v39). RDMA queue pairs are flapping briefly during the spike window.
noah: also saw TCP retransmits increase at the same time — guessing offloads + driver/firmware combo causing edge latency under load.
ops-sre: quick mitigation we can do right now: 1) reduce the batching window target to droppeak for next 2h, 2) pin offending pods to alternate racks (tor-5/tor-9), 3) enable per-TOR QoS to prioritize RDMA/IB traffic.
sara: good call. can we pin with a topology-affinity override until we patch?
noah: yes, pushing a single topology override now for the heaviest queues. `kubectl patch` applied to the q-serving deployment — pinned ~40% of traffic off rack-8.
deploy-bot: deployment rollout started: q-serving topology-affinity patch (canary) — 4/12 pods rescheduled.
matt: ordering follow-ups: firmware sync for 8-6 (matt@oncall), revert partial MTU change until we confirm jumbo config on ToR (anya), run BPF packet-dump in peak window (noah).
anya: I'm going to rollback the Ansible change for rack-8 and add a preflight check to ensure ToR MTU matches host MTU.
noah: I'll capture `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/ew-spike-$(date +%s).pcap` during next window and share small pcap. planning to grep for fragmented=1 and RSTs.
ops-sre: long-term: create a health-check lint in CI that verifies RDMA/firmware/driver matrix and disallows half-rollouts of MTU. filing ticket INFRA-1128.
sara: thanks. temporary owner list: matt -> firmware, anya -> MTU/ansible, noah -> packet capture and analysis. ops-sre will coordinate the QoS change with networking.
anya: small note — enabling jumbo frames on cloud-hosted hosts might increase CPU for small packets, so we'll test perf after revert.
matt: agreed. plan: firmware patch on 8-6 tonight at 22:00 with a quick smoke test; if green we can re-enable jumbo with full TOC.
sara: :thumbsup: keep updates here. if anything spikes again, tag @ops-sre and I'll escalate. end of thread.
